title: Alor Setar Marathon 2026: A Homegrown Night Race Through Kedah's Capital
seo_title: Alor Setar Marathon 2026 Review: Course & Cut-Off
meta_description: An honest look at the Alor Setar Marathon 2026 — dates, fees, cut-off, and what Northern Runners' Kedah race weekend is really like.
dek: Northern Runners brings five distances to Dataran Pekan Rabu on 14–15 August 2026, pairing a generous 8-hour marathon cut-off with an evening flag-off designed to dodge Kedah's daytime heat.
verdict: This is a locally organized, community-scale road race rather than a bucket-list marathon: flat city-square start and finish, an evening flag-off that avoids the worst heat, and an unusually forgiving 8-hour cut-off for the full distance. Affordable entry fees and an experienced regional organizer behind several other Kedah and Perlis races make it approachable for newer marathoners and travelling Malaysian runners. Just don't expect major-marathon polish or a deep archive of independent race reports — go in with realistic, homegrown-event expectations.

sections.heading: What Is the Alor Setar Marathon 2026?
paragraphs: The Alor Setar Marathon 2026 runs on 14–15 August 2026, staged by Northern Runners out of Dataran Pekan Rabu in Alor Setar, Kedah, with five distance options ranging from a 1km fun run up through 5km, 10km, 21km and the full 42.195km marathon [1].

Entry fees for 2026 sit roughly between RM30 and RM120 depending on category, and by race weekend the event's registration windows across multiple platforms had already closed, which lines up with the event now showing a closed sign-up status [1,2].

sections.heading: Course, Distance and Cut-Off
paragraphs: Detailed route maps for the 2026 edition aren't widely published yet, but the event's own listings confirm the marathon and its four shorter companion races all start and finish at Dataran Pekan Rabu, the same civic square used by several other Northern Runners events in the city [1].

What is confirmed, and notable, is the cut-off: race details shared across Malaysian running channels put the full marathon's cut-off time at eight hours, a generous window that opens the distance to first-timers and slower finishers rather than only quicker club runners [3].

sections.heading: Timing and Conditions
paragraphs: Flag-off is scheduled for around 6:00pm on the Friday evening, pushing runners into the cooler overnight hours before the event window runs into Saturday morning — a scheduling choice that sidesteps the tropical midday heat that August in northern Peninsular Malaysia typically brings [1,3].

That evening-into-night structure also means logistics like lighting, marshalling and hydration points along a course run mostly in darkness matter more here than on a standard daytime city race, even though specific route-level detail on those elements for 2026 hasn't surfaced in public race reports [3].

sections.heading: Organisation and Track Record
paragraphs: Technical delivery is handled by Northern Runners, the same organizing team behind the Alor Setar Merdeka Half Marathon, the Menara Alor Setar International Run and the Kangar City Half Marathon, meaning this marathon debut sits inside an established regional race calendar rather than being a first-time production [1].

On the organizer's track record, the numbers are reassuring: the Alor Setar Merdeka Half Marathon's participation reportedly grew from about 1,000 runners to around 2,500 within a year, evidence the same team can scale up crowd handling and race-day logistics [6].
Independent listings sum up the outfit's broader reputation simply: Northern Runners "creates energetic, supportive events that bring people together and celebrate the joy of running" [5].

sections.heading: Atmosphere and Buzz
paragraphs: In the run-up to race weekend, Malaysia's running community treated this like any hyped local calendar entry — Threads and Telegram groups traded discount codes, countdown posts and reactions to the finisher medal reveal, with commenters calling the design out specifically [2,3].

That kind of informal chatter — codes, medal previews, cut-off talk — is the clearest available signal that this sits comfortably within Malaysia's crowded scene of city and state races rather than positioning itself as an international marathon draw; expect a grassroots, community-driven vibe over big-budget race production [2,3].

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If a flat, town-square-based course, an evening start built to avoid the heat, an 8-hour marathon cut-off and modest entry fees appeal to you, the Alor Setar Marathon is a sensible pick — especially for runners in northern Malaysia looking to add mileage without traveling to a bigger city race [1,3].

Temper expectations on the finer details: this is a technical-run, locally organized event, and detailed independent write-ups of the marathon-distance course itself are still thin, so it's worth leaning on the organizer's record from sister events — like the well-marshalled logistics reported at earlier Alor Setar road races — as your best available guide rather than a guarantee [4,5].
